plan: In a second-price auction (pay second-highest bid if I win), the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding my value ensures I win whenever my value exceeds both competitors' bids (guaranteeing non-negative profit) and lose otherwise, avoiding overpaying. Since payment is determined by the second-highest bid, not my own bid, there's no incentive to shade up or down. With no prior history in this single-round game, I'll bid my true value of $25 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction with independent private values. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value, since you pay the second-highest bid regardless of your own bid (as long as you win). Bidding above your value risks paying more than the item is worth if I win against a bid between my value and my bid; bidding below reduces chances of winning profitable trades. Therefore, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.

This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid). The dominant strategy in this format is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win against a bid between my value and my bid. Bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With a value of $9, bidding $9 ensures I only win when profitable and pay a fair price if I do.
